purpose: gauss_sieve algorithm control — tests whether variance_ratio > 1 is bgj1-specific or algorithm-independent

key_results.N_vectors_note: gauss_sieve produces variable N per run (18098, 18469, 18848); bgj1 produced constant N=17919

run_environment.qemu_emulation: linux/amd64 on Darwin arm64 (Apple Silicon via Docker QEMU)

git.dirty_note: BATCH-e87ab3 task directory is untracked (??); script is self-contained, no repo imports

protocol_deviations.deviation: gauss_sieve produces variable N_vectors per run (18098, 18469, 18848), unlike bgj1_sieve which produced constant N=17919
protocol_deviations.impact: empirical Var[T_N] conflates score variance with N-count variance; the normalization N_run0=18469 may not equal mean(N). Law of total variance: Var[T_N] = E[N]*Var[s_i] + Var[N]*(E[s_i])^2. This is an inherent property of gauss_sieve, not a script error.

protocol_deviations.deviation: mean_TN_gauss (7635.72) is higher than bgj1 mean (7551-7554), consistent with higher N_vectors in gauss_sieve runs (mean N ≈ 18512 vs bgj1 N=17919)
protocol_deviations.impact: Cross-algorithm T_N comparison is confounded by different N; ratio uses within-gauss normalization

anomalies.detail: variance_ratio_gauss = 2.764 (p=4.92e-10, n=50). The gauss_sieve ratio is substantially larger than bgj1 batches (1.39, 1.53). The RC-3 cross-run correlation r=0.30, p=0.14 is not significant at alpha=0.05. N_vectors varies per run (18098–18848).
anomalies.impact: Observation recorded. No finding stated. For Coordinator / Reviewer assessment.

anomalies.detail: gauss_sieve terminates in 14-17s per run at dim=60, similar to bgj1_sieve. Feared slowness did not materialize; all 50 runs completed with 13 min of sieve time.

executor_assessment.note: N_vectors variability is a substantive methodological point requiring Coordinator attention before interpreting the ratio.
